Step 1: $R$ is strictly dominated by $C$ for player 2 ($3>1$, $2>1$, $1>0$), remove $R$.
Step 2: now $D$ is strictly dominated by $M$ ($2>1$, $2>1$), remove $D$.
Step 3: no more strictly dominated strategies. Survivors: $\{U,M\} \times \{L,C\}$.
Best responses: against $L$ player 1 picks $T$, against $R$ picks $B$; against $T$ player 2 picks $L$, against $B$ picks $R$. Pure NE: $(T,L)$ and $(B,R)$.
Player 1 indifferent gives $p$: $4p = 2(1-p)$, $p = 1/3$. Player 2 indifferent gives $q$: $2q = 4(1-q)$, $q = 2/3$.
Dominant strategies are always best, so $s^*$ is NE and nothing else can be.
